claims.claim: The user interface and control layouts are described as unintuitive, clunky, and difficult to navigate.

citations.review_text:
The controls for this game are cooked. The controller layout and limited alternate options are just awful to engage with. 

The keyboard and mouse combo and UI list nightmare, is so unintuitive, so utterly un-thought out, you spend most of the tutorial fussing with lists and holding random keys within lists, to further action or to que stuff. Only to order AI to play the game for you. or have the context sensitive actions produce a yell from you with the slightest mouse-point deviation.

What is this? How does this pass for user interface? What am I missing; that people like to engage with this dogshit effort?

single_points.text: One reviewer says the in-game mod menu is pretty buggy and asks for your email and a verification code every time you open it.

citation.review_text:
Overall, the game isn't as bad as my review might make it sound, but there are a few caveats. First, it’s not as realistic as some reviews claim, and it suffers from stability issues—at least in my experience. It often struggles with rendering and can look blurry in certain scenes, though it's manageable.

The game has a ton of mods that fix some of the common complaints, like the censorship the devs added for console distribution. However, despite the great mod selection, the in-game mod menu is pretty buggy. Every time you open it, it asks for your email and a verification code from mod.io, which gets really annoying. On top of that, there is no clear way to track installation progress when downloading mods.

If you're an Arma fan or just looking for a truly realistic game, I’d recommend checking out Operator. I really enjoy it, though since it's in Early Access, there are only about 20 hours of playable missions. Still, it offers a massive amount of deep, advanced weapon customization.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that solo play features an AI squad that struggles with basic tasks, such as failing to secure subjects when ordered or mishandling flashbangs at doors.

citations.review_text: Very fun concept with execution somewhat falling short. Enough fun to play through the game and DLCs, but the AI team in solo play reminds of old school game jank. Team constantly fails to secure subjects, even when directly ordered, and frequently hits doorframes with flashbangs. I've died more from the team failing to execute basic commands than any other source in the game. Solo play is a 50/50 split of intense, immersive gameplay and feeling like your leading your leading "special" operators through their first real world mission.

Overall I guess I recommend this game to play its so fun but it makes me so fucking incredibly frustrated and tired of it when you try to S rank or get achievements its not only hard but unpredictably unfair to the point where you could fuckin crawl all around the map as slow and carefully as you can and play the same mission for like an hour just to open a door and blow the fuck up with your entire team, boom whole hour of my life for nothing. You also don't stand a fucking chance against the AI because either your team doesn't listen to you at all or the enemies just run around everywhere while aim botting you its almost impossible to combat against them unless you either catch them off guard or throw 50 stingers and another 50 flashbangs because if they know your there and are waiting for you and there's more than 3 of them in a room, you and your team are FUCKED. I HATE THIS GAME SO MUCH but I have fun playing it when its not bullshitting the fuck out of me.

This game really does a lot of things right, but the enemy AI is the worst of any tactical shooter I've played since they became a thing. Omniscient AI with literal 360 degree vision that can sprint at speeds that would make Usain Bolt raise an eyebrow while firing their weapons with perfect accuracy are not fun or interesting to fight against. Every gunfight is simply a roll of the dice. Will my load of 12 gauge buckshot fired from 5 meters drop this suspect, or will he spinbot me in the head the moment I fire? There's no way to know. At least on PC you can mod out some of these ridiculous behaviors to a degree, but that shouldn't be my job. I shouldn't have to hunt down mods to make the AI behave in a semi-believable way. 

I've already put too many hours into this game and I'll probably put more, but don't make the same mistakes I did. Stay away from this nonsense.
